title: Self-reference: the diagonal lemma and undefinability of truth

based_on.title: An Introduction to Gödel's Theorems, second edition, corrected Logic Matters reprint

summary: Construct sentences that describe their own codes, and prove that no arithmetic formula defines truth for all arithmetic sentences.
abstract: Can an arithmetic sentence make a claim about its own code? The diagonal lemma constructs such sentences: for any arithmetic property of codes, it produces a sentence that Robinson arithmetic proves equivalent to that property of its own code. The construction uses ordinary formula substitution, with no new self-referential symbols. Applying it to a proposed truth predicate proves Tarski’s theorem: arithmetic cannot define truth for all its own sentences. It also shows that no consistent extension of Robinson arithmetic can prove every proposed truth biconditional. These are precise limits on what formulas can express and what formal systems can establish.
